technical_and_design_decisions: Target Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3 baseline, consistent with the referenced Spring ecosystem.

Kafka and Rabbit JUnit @Rule test fixtures will each be extracted into a dedicated Git repository and published as versioned Maven test artifacts so other projects can consume them via a test-scoped dependency.

Platform-neutral Admin REST API will be implemented behind a deployer SPI abstraction with separate implementations for Cloud Foundry, YARN, and Lattice, sharing a single controller layer to guarantee consistent API behavior.
A shared REST API contract test suite (Spring Cloud Contract / MockMvc based) will be executed against all platform implementations to verify consistency at build time.
Library artifacts will be registered as Maven coordinates in the artifact registry and resolved at stream creation/deployment time for include/exclude statements.
Named channels will be supported via a DSL extension (':channelName' as an endpoint) with binding handled by the existing binder abstraction, enabling pipelines without source or sink modules.
Stream name uniqueness will be enforced at the service layer plus a unique constraint at the repository/persistence layer, returning a clear conflict error.
The Kinesis source module will be built on Spring Integration AWS / AWS SDK and tested against LocalStack to avoid requiring live AWS resources.
StreamController coverage will use MockMvc-based web layer tests plus repository/service integration tests wired into the CI build.
assumptions: The work is performed by a single developer (myself) experienced with the Spring ecosystem; effort excludes elapsed calendar time and wait states.
One workday equals 8 hours of focused development work.
An existing Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream codebase, build system (Maven), and CI infrastructure (e.g., GitHub Actions/Jenkins) are available to build upon.
Test environments or emulators are accessible for Cloud Foundry, YARN, Lattice, Kafka, RabbitMQ, and Kinesis (LocalStack).
Requirements are REST API and DSL level only; no UI/shell changes are included except where strictly implied.
Newly created repositories inherit standard Spring project conventions, so release/publishing setup is mostly configuration reuse.
Documentation effort covers reference documentation and release notes for the increment only.
No clarification is available; ambiguous scope is interpreted reasonably and recorded here.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, confirm architectural approach (deployer SPI, DSL changes, registry extension), and produce the detailed design used by subsequent activities.
U1: Create the Kafka test-fixtures repository, extract the Kafka @Rule/support classes from the existing codebase, and refactor them into a reusable module.

activities.activity_name: Kafka fixtures build, publishing, and consumer migration
activities.activity_description: U1: Configure Maven build, CI, and artifact publishing for the Kafka fixtures repo; migrate existing projects to consume the published test artifact.
U2: Create the Rabbit test-fixtures repository and extract the Rabbit @Rule/support classes into a reusable module.

activities.activity_name: Rabbit fixtures build, publishing, and consumer migration
activities.activity_description: U2: Configure build, CI, and publishing for the Rabbit fixtures repo; migrate existing consumers to the published test artifact.

activities.activity_name: Design platform-neutral Admin REST API and deployer SPI
activities.activity_description: U3: Define the common controller layer and deployer SPI contracts so the Admin REST APIs behave identically across Cloud Foundry, YARN, and Lattice.
U3: Implement the Cloud Foundry deployer/admin integration behind the SPI, including unit tests.
U3: Implement the YARN deployer/admin integration behind the SPI, including unit tests.
U3: Implement the Lattice deployer/admin integration behind the SPI, including unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Cross-platform REST API contract test suite
activities.activity_description: U3: Build a shared contract test suite executed against all three platform implementations to guarantee consistent REST API behavior at build time.
U4: Extend the artifact registry to register and resolve artifacts as libraries (Maven coordinates), including persistence and REST endpoints.
U4: Implement include/exclude statement handling so registered libraries can be referenced during stream definition and deployment.
U4: Unit and integration tests covering library registration, resolution, and include/exclude behavior.
U5: Extend the stream DSL parser to accept named channels as pipeline endpoints, enabling definitions without source or sink modules.

activities.activity_name: Named channel binding and deployment logic
activities.activity_description: U5: Implement binding of named channels through the binder abstraction during stream deployment, including validation of channel references.
U5: Integration tests verifying end-to-end pipelines composed via named channels across source/processor/sink combinations.
U6: Add MockMvc-based web layer tests and contract-style tests for StreamController to verify API contracts at build time in CI.
U7: Enforce unique stream names with service-layer validation and a persistence-level unique constraint, returning a clear conflict error, plus tests.
U8: Implement the Kinesis source module (based on Spring Integration AWS / AWS SDK) so it can be used as a source in streaming pipelines, including configuration properties.
U8: Integration tests for the Kinesis source module using LocalStack, covering record consumption, checkpointing, and error handling.
Update reference documentation for named channels, library registration, Kinesis source, platform admin APIs, and the extracted test fixtures; write release notes.

activities.activity_name: Final integration, code review, and release packaging
activities.activity_description: Cross-story integration, full regression run in CI, code review rework, and packaging/versioning of all deliverables of the increment.
